newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek brokers upset with commission's intervention.
newsitem.headline: Greek brokers upset with commission's intervention.

text.p: Greek brokers, upset over the Athens bourse's freefall on Thursday, blasted the Capital Market Commission for what they said were attempts to police the market with improper statements.

"The bourse's freefall proved once more how sensitive the market can be to interventions by capital market officials who... theorise at improper times without taking responsibility for their actions," The Association of Athens Stock Exchange Member Brokers (SMEHA) said in a statement.
The reaction came after capital market commission president Stavros Thomadakis warned against rumour-based investment decisions on Wednesday, fearing speculative market conditions at the exchange.
The bourse plunged more than 7.0 percent at mid-session on Thursday as investors, spooked by the surprise warning headed for the exit sign, driving many large-cap stocks limit down.
Greek shares closed 5.95 percent or 86.44 points lower after panic selling brought the benchmark index down to 1,367.16 on heavy volume of 30.8 billion drachmas.
"Authorities should respect the operating rules of the exchange and they should avoid policing with uncalled for statements in the name of investor protection," SMEHA said.
It said the capital market commission's role was to supervise the market within the law and not substitute professional investment advisors.
"It is common knowledge that stock markets operate based on the laws of supply and demand and it is these forces that influence prices," SMEHA added.
It urged the investment public to show self-restraint and avoid panic selling at a time when macroeconomic fundamentals looked positive, with inflation at its lowest level in 25 years.
January CPI-based inflation dropped to 6.8 percent year-on-year.
The commission's president, who denied market rumours he was resigning over the reaction, reiterated on Thursday that his comments aimed to protect the public.
"All I wanted to do was to recommend calmness in a climate of enthusiasm. The mission of the capital market commission is to secure normal market conditions and protect investors," Thomadakis said.
But his comments reversed a recent rally, with investors hammering its driving force, the large caps they were previously buying at a frothing pace. Banks tumbled 7.27 percent.
A good chunk of market capitalisation was wiped out with many market watchers pondering the overall effect on market sentiment and others licking their wounds.

Conservative member of parliament Manolis Kefaloyannis asked National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou in an open letter whether the intervention was due to the government's inability to attract funds to its March 1 treasury paper issue.
"How can the capital market commission president, who has a mandate to protect the investing public, make statements that cause the exact opposite?" he asked.

Asked to explain the rationale for the intervention, Thomadakis told reporters on Wednesday: "We do not believe or wish to point out that the stock market is overvalued," noting that the critical element in terms of investor protection was "self-protection". --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
